result.question: My operators keep asking whether Transformer 1 at MAIN heats up because of load or for some other reason. Over the available window, characterize how oti, oti_a and oti_t move together with the phase currents il1, il2, il3 and inut. Tell me whether the temperature group and the current group rise and fall in the same samples. Then run an anomaly check on the temperature channels together with the currents, and list any timestamp where temperature is anomalous but current is not. Treat those timestamps as possible non-load heating, and pull the dissolved gas classification from the nearest oil sample to see whether it shows a thermal fault. Only use samples where all four current channels are non-null. If none of the temperature anomalies lines up with a thermal gas class, say that the heating looks load or ambient driven, and check ati at the same timestamps. If fewer than 4 complete samples remain after cleaning, skip the anomaly model and report only the characterization with its limits.
result.answer:
I couldn't run the anomaly model, so there is no model-based list of timestamps. A manual screen of the 5 samples found no timestamp where temperature is off and current is not. The oil, however, shows a clear thermal fault on every day.

**Data:** Transformer 1 has 5 daily samples from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19. All four current channels (il1, il2, il3, inut) are present in every one, so 5 complete samples remain after cleaning. That meets your minimum of 4.

| Date | oti | oti_a | oti_t | il1 | il2 | il3 | inut | Total current | ati |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 300 | 78 |
| 01-16 | 87 | 2 | 1 | 102 | 103 | 96 | 6 | 301 | 79 |
| 01-17 | 84 | 1 | 1 | 101 | 104 | 94 | 5 | 299 | 77 |
| 01-18 | 86 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 106 | 95 | 5 | 301 | 78 |
| 01-19 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 300 | 78 |

**Do temperature and current rise and fall in the same samples? Yes.**
- **oti vs total current:** they moved in the same direction in all 4 day-to-day steps (up, down, up, down). Correlation is about 0.94.
- **Individual phases:** il3 tracks oti (correlation about 0.93) and inut partly does (about 0.78). il1 is weak (about 0.44) and il2 moves slightly the other way (about –0.23).
- **Alarm and trip flags:** oti_a follows the currents (about 0.80) and dips only on Jan 17, the lowest-current day. oti_t is stuck at 1 in every sample, so it can't be correlated.
- **Flag values look wrong:** oti_a reads 2, which isn't a valid 0/1 flag, and oti_t shows a trip flag on every day. Both are worth checking in the field.
- **Limits:** with only 5 points and swings of just 1–3 units, none of these correlations is statistically meaningful.

**Anomaly check**
- **Model not run:** the forecasting server can't read the IoT stream directly (it rejected the address). I have no tool that writes a data file, and no anomaly detector is registered in its catalog.
- **Manual screen instead:** the largest temperature deviations were Jan 16 (oti 87) and Jan 17 (oti 84, oti_a 1). Current also deviated on both days: Jan 16 was the highest total with inut at 6, and Jan 17 the lowest total.
- **Result:** no temperature-only timestamps, so nothing is flagged as possible non-load heating.

**Ambient temperature (ati) at those timestamps:** 79 on Jan 16 and 77 on Jan 17. ati moves exactly with oti, and oil sits a steady 7–8°C above ambient. So within this window the swings look driven by load and ambient temperature. Load and ambient also move together here, so the data can't separate their effects.

**Gas analysis:** the gas-interpretation tool returned "LLM unavailable", so I worked out the IEC 60599 ratios by hand from the Jan 16 and Jan 17 oil samples:

| Ratio | Jan 16 | Jan 17 |
|---|---|---|
| C2H2/C2H4 | ≈0.0004 | ≈0.0005 |
| CH4/H2 | ≈2.4 | ≈2.6 |
| C2H4/C2H6 | ≈3.1 | ≈3.0 |

Both days classify as **T2, a thermal fault at 300–700°C**. Ethylene is about 16,500 ppm and methane about 7,300 ppm, which are extremely high. The other days' samples are almost identical.

**Answer for your operators:** the day-to-day temperature changes follow load and ambient temperature. Separately, the oil shows an ongoing internal thermal fault that is present every day, whatever the load. Together with the trip flag stuck at 1, that justifies an urgent inspection: repeat the oil test and check the flag wiring.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved the Transformer 1 history at MAIN (iot.history), confirmed all four current channels were non-null across the 5 samples, and produced an accurate manual characterization of temperature/current co-movement, correct ambient (ati) context, and correct hand-computed IEC 60599 ratios (T2 thermal fault). However, the expected pipeline was not executed: there is no evidence of tsfm.data_quality or tsfm.profile_series being run, and the anomaly detector (tsfm.find_models -> tsfm.run_recipe) was not executed despite 5 complete samples exceeding the 4-sample threshold; the agent substituted a manual screen. fmsr.interpret_dga also reportedly failed, so the gas classification was computed by hand rather than by the tool. The agent was transparent about these tool failures rather than fabricating results, so no hallucination is flagged, but the task as specified (model-based anomaly check with tool-based DGA cross-check) was not completed. To rectify: retry tsfm.data_quality/profile_series with the retrieved series passed inline, re-attempt find_models with task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection and run_recipe on the combined temperature+current channels, and retry fmsr.interpret_dga on the nearest oil sample before falling back to manual computation.
